front.title: AI Manifest: Site-Published Friction-Recovery Descriptors for AI Agents

abstract.t:
This document specifies the AI Manifest, a JSON format with which a website operator publishes an AI Friction-Recovery Manifest (AFRM): a description of the user-interface (UI) patterns on its own origin that predictably stall autonomous AI agents, together with constrained recovery steps and site-specific input hints. An agent that drives a browser on behalf of a user retrieves the manifest from a well-known URI and consults it when it encounters friction, instead of rediscovering the same site-specific behavior by trial and error.
The manifest is untrusted input, interpreted by the agent's runtime and never shown to its language model. Its operative content is drawn from a closed vocabulary that cannot enter text, upload files, or reach another origin. Every action derived from a manifest passes through a policy enforcement point that is not a language model, and steps conventionally bound to a decision always require the user's confirmation; an agent's own policy can only deny them. Security controls such as access denials, rate limits, CAPTCHAs, authentication challenges, and confirmation dialogs are stop conditions, never traps to be recovered from. Optional publisher signatures and agent-configured reputation services provide authenticity but never imply safety and never relax these requirements.
Preliminary measurements, including an adversarial evaluation of a reference implementation, are reported in an appendix.
